Wyandot of Anderdon Nation

The Wyandot of Anderdon’s public history follows families around the Detroit River region. A federal conservation report documents collaborative work at Six Points.

Names & relationshipsThe Nation’s public pages identify a Wyandot community with an elected council and describe its nonprofit corporate form. Wyandotte Nation’s history separately names the Anderdon community in Michigan. This outline keeps the community and organization context visible and does not equate corporate status, federal acknowledgment, shared peoplehood or individual citizenship.
A source guide for a deeper dive.This entry provides a brief orientation and an organized reading path. A comprehensive deep dive has not yet been completed. Follow the annotated sources and distinguish primary community accounts from outside reference material.

01

Reading the community’s own history

Anderdon’s public history describes movement to Detroit in the early eighteenth century, settlement near Amherstburg and continuing family histories on both sides of the Detroit River. It also describes language and historical-archive work. The page’s account of a project ending in 2025 is retained as a dated report, with its later continuation still to investigate.

Read the sources [1] Wyandot of Anderdon Nation

02

Land stewardship at Six Points

The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service’s 2022 report describes cooperation with the Wyandot community, the International Wildlife Refuge Alliance and local volunteers at Six Points. It reports removing invasive plants to restore more than five acres of wetlands. This specific public conservation activity adds another way into the community’s relationship with place; the report is not a current visitor-access guide.

Read the sources [2] U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service

Community historical synthesisWyandot of Anderdon NationSource 1

History — A Short History of the Wyandot of Anderdon ↗

The community’s public history follows movements around the Detroit River and describes later efforts in language, history and archives. Read as its situated synthesis rather than a universal Wyandot history.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Entire publicly exposed Short History body read, including expanded paragraphs about the Detroit River, Anderdon Reserve, southeast Michigan and cultural work. No login, citizen-only Facebook page or restricted material accessed; embedded Prezi timelines not inspected. The page anticipates a grant ending in 2025, so that project is not described as currently running. Underlying treaties, family archives and legal claims were not verified.

Review recorded: October 27, 2026

Federal conservation activity reportU.S. Fish and Wildlife ServiceSource 2

Coastal Program 2022 Accomplishment Report — Supporting Tribal Communities: Michigan ↗

Publication: 2022

A concrete account of wetland restoration at the Six Points Wyandot Tribal Heritage Site, identifying the Wyandot community and its collaborators. It complements the community history with a dated activity record.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Physical PDF page 11, a spread printed 19-20, full Michigan/Six Points body and image caption read as extracted text and rendered pixels. Regional headline statistics were not attributed to this site. Other projects and later outcomes were not reviewed.

Review recorded: October 27, 2026
